meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble, misfortune' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble, misfortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну, допустим, я жулик. А ты жадина и не помогаешь людям в беде.
examples.trans: All right, let's say I'm a crook. But you're greedy, and you don't help people in trouble.

meanings.note: Neuter abstract noun. Common neuter noun meaning 'well-being, prosperity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They care about the well-being of the children.

examples.text: Я думала о благополучии наших детей.
examples.trans: I thought about the well-being of our children.

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
short forms виноват / виновата / виноваты are used for 'it's my/your fault'

examples.text: Я ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: I'm not to blame for anything.

meanings.note: идти во власть = go into government
идти во власть = go into government

examples.trans: People need to go into government themselves.

examples.text: Самим идти во власть? Что это значит?
examples.trans: Go into government themselves? What does that mean?
The grandson of a collaborator is clawing his way into power!

meanings.note: Plural only. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'боры'). Common substantive noun meaning 'election' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is running in the election.

examples.text: У меня много дел. Выборы мэра…
examples.trans: I've got a lot to do. The mayoral election...

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: 'голову оторвать' = to tear someone's head off
meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: imperative держи! when handing something over
imperative держи! when handing something over
Держи его!. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hold'.

examples.trans: Here you go, this is for you.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cheap, inexpensive').

examples.text: Я не хочу играть в этот дешёвый спектакль.
examples.trans: I do not want to play in this cheap performance.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.en: to use, make use of, utilize
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'пользовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to use, utilize'.

examples.text: Каким образом мы можем это использовать?

examples.trans: To make use of an opportunity.

examples.text: Ты используешь нас ради своей власти!
examples.trans: You are using us for the sake of your power!

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

meanings.note: Кричать на + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to shout', paired with 'крикнуть'.

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.

молчать.gloss: to be silent, to say nothing

meanings.en: to be silent, to keep quiet
meanings.note: почему ты молчишь? = why aren't you saying anything?

examples.text: Ну что ты молчишь? Ты толстый, ты не спортсмен!
examples.trans: Well, why are you so quiet? You're fat, you're no athlete!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: usually in short form обязан/обязана + dative + instrumental

examples.trans: You are obliged to come on time.

examples.text: Ты выпустишь меня под подписку о невыезде. И ты мне больше ничем не обязан.
examples.trans: You'll release me on a travel ban. And you won't owe me anything anymore.

meanings.note: перестань(те)! = stop it!, oh come on!

examples.text: Да перестаньте! Я двадцать лет в карты не играла.
examples.trans: Oh, stop it! I haven't played cards for twenty years.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: + dative of the person: поверить ему

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

при.gloss: in the presence of, in front of; at, under

meanings.en: in the presence of, in front of (a person)
meanings.note: + prepositional: при нём, при детях
+ prepositional. Core Russian prep meaning 'in the presence of, in front of; at, under' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Why did you just say that in front of him?

examples.text: Не говори об этом при детях.
examples.trans: Don't talk about this in front of the children.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'мерный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('exemplary, model').

examples.text: Мне нужна примерная семья для выборов.
examples.trans: I need an exemplary family for the election.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for the sake of' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Work, work. It's all for us.

meanings.note: Cause ruin to a family or thing. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'рушить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to destroy, to ruin', paired with 'разрушать'.

examples.text: Ты разрушил мою семью своими фотографиями!
examples.trans: You destroyed my family with your photos!

examples.text: Ты разрушил такой прекрасный и сентиментальный момент!
examples.trans: You ruined such a wonderful and sentimental moment!

meanings.note: Comparative of рано. Core Russian adv meaning 'earlier, previously, used to' in everyday speech.

examples.text: В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Uncle Misha used to live in my room.
There used to be an old park here.

examples.text: Подождите. В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Wait. Uncle Misha used to live in my room.

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.
Рядом с + instrumental. Core Russian adv meaning 'next to, nearby, beside' in everyday speech.
Adverb of place. Core Russian adv meaning 'next to, nearby, beside' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.
Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: To do with the family. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емейный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('family').

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так, семья Самсоновых. Он строитель, она медсестра.
examples.trans: Right, the Samsonov family. He's a builder, she's a nurse.

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: On stage. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пектакль'). Common masculine noun meaning 'performance, play, show' in everyday Russian.
Figurative dramatic display. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пектакль'). Common masculine noun meaning 'performance, play, show' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, ну что же вы делаете? Прекратите этот спектакль!
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, what are you doing? Stop this performance!

examples.text: Я не хочу играть в этот дешёвый спектакль.
examples.trans: I do not want to play in this cheap performance.

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: К счастью = fortunately. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'частье'). Common neuter noun meaning 'happiness, good fortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Happiness is getting closer, almost here!

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Кому = at someone (dative). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лыбаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to smile', paired with 'улыбнуться'.

examples.trans: Nothing! He just sits there smiling.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things
Чужой человек = a stranger. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('someone else's, foreign').

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
